English: Open Table
A simple gathering place where traders lay out their wares on cloth or boards, forming the bare beginnings of a market among the Israelite nomads.
Barter Patch
A rough square of trampled earth, where Israelite clans meet to exchange goods, livestock, and stories. Trust and unity are fostered among the tribes in this communal patch.
Traders Tent
Simple canvas tents shelter merchants and their wares from the elements, attracting more traders and fostering a sense of community among Israelite clans.
Merchants Pavilion
A large communal tent, reinforced with wooden beams, where Israelite merchants gather for both commerce and council. Trade thrives under its canvas.
Market Stand
Wooden stalls and awnings now line the market grounds, offering shelter for goods and drawing in traders from distant tribes. Organization and prosperity increase among the Israelites.
Exchange Room
A sturdy wooden structure, guarded and organized, where coin and contracts begin to supplement barter among the Israelites. Trade with outsiders becomes more frequent.
Market Hall
A grand semi-permanent hall of timber and stone, the market now hosts merchants from far and wide, and Israelite clans gather in unity and prosperity.
Guild Pavilion
A vast, ornate tented structure where merchant guilds are formed and Israelite clan leaders convene to adjudicate trade disputes and alliances.
Grand Market Room
A permanent structure of carved stone and timber, bustling with traders, scribes, and envoys. The center of Israelite commerce and unity, renowned across the steppes.
Israelite Grand Market
The pride of the Israelite nomads: a legendary market complex, where all tribes convene for trade, diplomacy, and celebration. The heart of unity and prosperity for the Jewish people.
